newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Greens expect help on social cuts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Greens expect help on social cuts.

text.p: Australian Greens senator Bob Brown said on Friday he was confident other minor parties could be convinced to oppose in the Senate some of the government's proposed social security changes.
The two Greens senators confirmed that they would oppose social security measures from the government's budget worth about A$750 million over three years.
"The other senators have variously indicated that they're opposed to the harsher side of the government's measures," Brown told reporters.
Brown later told Reuters he believed the "harsher measures" included extending the non-payment waiting period to 26 weeks from 12 weeks for people moving to lower employment prospects.
They also included changes to the disability allowance and allowances given to the unemployed to help them find jobs.
"We certainly will be consulting with the other components in the Senate," Brown said. "On some of these issues, some of them have already made comments about their unacceptability."
The government needs the support of at least two non-government senators to get budget measures through the upper house.
"The Greens are going to use whatever powers we have in the Senate, and they are considerable, to blunt this attack on the social security system," Brown said.
He said the Greens would also approach the government about their concerns over the proposed changes and hoped for a response before Senate debate started.
The legislation is currently in the lower house of parliament, the House of Representatives, and is expected to be introduced into the upper house Senate before the end of calendar 1996.
